gloss: beef (or pork) and egg rice bowl

definitions.gloss: beef (or pork) and egg rice bowl
definitions.explanation: A rice bowl dish topped with sliced beef or pork simmered with onions in a sweet soy-based broth, then bound with beaten egg. Named in contrast to {親子丼|おやこどん}, which uses chicken and egg.

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}に{他人丼|たにんどん}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a beef and egg rice bowl for lunch.

examples.japanese: {他人丼|たにんどん}は{親子丼|おやこどん}と{似|に}ているが、{肉|にく}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Tanindon is similar to oyakodon, but the meat is different.

examples.japanese: {関西|かんさい}では{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}の{他人丼|たにんどん}が{定番|ていばん}メニューだ。
examples.english: In the Kansai region, beef tanindon is a standard menu item.

notes:
The name is a playful contrast with {親子丼|おやこどん} (parent-and-child bowl). In {親子丼|おやこどん}, the chicken ({親|おや}, parent) and egg ({子|こ}, child) are related, so they are "parent and child." In {他人丼|たにんどん}, the meat (beef or pork) and egg are from different animals, so they are "{他人|たにん}" (strangers/unrelated people).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {他人丼|たにんどん}を{作|つく}る: to make a tanindon
- {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}の{他人丼|たにんどん}: beef tanindon
- {豚肉|ぶたにく}の{他人丼|たにんどん}: pork tanindon

REGIONAL NOTE:
{他人丼|たにんどん} is more commonly known in the Kansai region. In Kanto, it is sometimes called {開化丼|かいかどん} (civilization bowl), a name dating back to the Meiji era when eating beef became popular.

RELATED WORDS:
- {親子丼|おやこどん}: chicken and egg rice bowl — the "parent-and-child" counterpart
- {牛丼|ぎゅうどん}: beef bowl — simmered beef on rice without egg
- {丼|どんぶり}: rice bowl dish — the general category
